text:
Dev Patel: hey folks — support enablement for Hosted canary rollouts GA. we’re getting early Qs from a couple customers and i want a tight troubleshooting + FAQ doc we can paste from. what are the top things to check when a customer says “my canary looks wrong” (split, metrics, latency regression, etc)? also: best escalation path (SRE vs platform vs telemetry).

Owen Phillips: +1. i’m seeing 3 recurring themes even in beta:
1) “traffic split isn’t what i set”
2) “candidate is slower / more 5xx but dashboards don’t show it”
3) “how do i rollback safely w/ streaming sessions?”

Allison Grant: for (1) first thing: ask them what they mean by split. are they looking at request count or token count? and over what window.
- request-based split is what routing does.
- token volume can skew if candidate produces longer outputs.
also: confirm they’re looking at *variant-tagged* dashboards, not the route aggregate.

Allison Grant: we have a draft runbook for pause/rollback that support can follow (internal): https://redwoodinference.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGPLAT/pages/hosted-rollout-pause-and-rollback-runbook
(we should probably pull a short “support version” out of it).

Logan Wright: re dashboards/metrics: common gotcha is ingestion delay + windowing.
- per-variant metrics are emitted at request end; for long streams you don’t see completion-based counts until stream completes.
- dashboards default to 5m/15m windows; if they just changed weights, it takes a few mins for stabilization.
if they want near-real-time, suggest looking at the “Rollout change events” overlay + last 30m.

Nadia Rahman: cost/token metrics: another gotcha is “max token cost delta” guardrail uses *metered* token cost (post-normalization), not the raw input/output tokens they see client-side.
so if they’re comparing to their own client tokenization, numbers won’t match perfectly.
if they ask “why did rollout pause due to cost delta”, tell them to export the per-variant cost panel + compare p50/p95 token cost per request.

Sean Gallagher: escalation guidance from SRE side:
- if customer sees elevated 5xx/timeouts and it’s ongoing: instruct immediate pause (force candidate to 0%).
- if pause doesn’t take effect within propagation SLO (couple mins) OR only some regions seem updated => page SRE (we can check staleness/propagation).
- if it’s “split looks off” but service healthy => file ticket + route to #eng-platform.
we should define a simple decision tree support can follow.

Marissa Cole: fwiw for GA we’re trying to keep default UX safe: can’t set 100% candidate without guardrails unless you have elevated perms. so when support sees a customer at 100% candidate and unhappy, also check if they intentionally bypassed guardrails (and whether they’re on the plan that allows it).

Jordan Lee: troubleshooting checklist for “split isn’t matching %”:
1) confirm effective routing policy (Console has “Preview effective routing”). customers often edit account-level policy + expect route-level to override.
2) check if stickiness is enabled. with request-hash stickiness, small sample sizes can look skewed.
3) confirm they’re not pinning a variant via custom header / SDK setting (some internal users do this).
4) check retries: retries reuse the same variant selection (by design). so transient failures can cluster.

Chloe Martin: + on (1) — we’ve seen cases where they updated rollout weights but were looking at a different route env (staging vs prod) or wrong region filter.
for support: ask for:
- route ID
- rollout ID
- which region(s)
- timestamp of change
then we can query the rollout policy history and see the version + propagation status.

Rafael Mendes: adding practical steps for “pause/rollback didn’t work” (support-safe):
- in Console, hit Pause -> verify status shows “Paused” and candidate weight shows 0%.
- wait 2–3 mins.
- verify via dashboard: baseline request rate should return to ~100%.
- if still seeing candidate traffic, ask if they have multiple rollouts (account-level + route-level). effective policy preview will show both.
if still weird, escalate to SRE w/ route + rollout + region.

Dev Patel: can we capture a crisp FAQ for streaming? customers keep asking if one chat session can switch variants mid-stream.

Jordan Lee: answer: no mixing within a single streaming request. selection happens at request start and is pinned for the lifetime of that request. retries also reuse that selection.
BUT: a “session” across multiple requests (like multi-turn chat) is not automatically pinned unless they enable sticky routing, or they pass a stable key (depending on SDK). so if they want consistent variant per user/session, they should use stickiness.

Allison Grant: i’ll add: if they’re doing client-side parallel calls (fanout), stickiness might not help if key varies. we should tell them to pick a deterministic key (user_id / conversation_id).

Logan Wright: on metrics for streaming: if they’re monitoring error rate, note that “client disconnect” can count as non-5xx depending on how they terminate. so “it failed” might not show in 5xx if it’s a cancel.
we do have a panel for cancel/abort rate by variant; support can point them there.

Owen Phillips: can we list common customer questions + short answers? draft:
- Q: why does candidate show fewer requests than %?
  A: sample size / stickiness / windowing / change just applied.
- Q: why does token cost not match our tokens?
  A: metered tokens differ; use Redwood cost metric.
- Q: can we rollback instantly?
  A: pause sets candidate to 0; propagation within minutes; if not, escalate.
- Q: can we see who changed rollout?
  A: audit timeline in Console + audit events export (enterprise).

Marissa Cole: + add “what guardrails exist?”
- error-rate threshold
- latency threshold (p95)
- max token cost delta
- optional quality gate (if enabled)
Support should always ask which guardrails they configured, bc “rollout didn’t auto-pause” often means they didn’t set any.

Sean Gallagher: please also include “when to ask for HAR / request IDs”.
if they say “candidate is worse”, ask for:
- 5–10 request IDs for baseline + candidate (if they have them)
- approximate time window
- whether they changed prompts at same time (happens a lot)
we can pull traces + compare.

Dev Patel: super helpful. action items i’ll take:
1) compile the decision tree + FAQ into a support macro.
2) add escalation table:
- routing/policy questions => #eng-platform (Jordan/Benji)
- metrics/dashboard oddities => #observability (Logan/Allison)
- propagation/partial region issues, ongoing customer impact => SRE oncall (Sean team)
3) link runbook + “creating canary in staging” doc for internal repro.

Chloe Martin: for internal repro doc: https://redwoodinference.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGPLAT/pages/creating-a-hosted-canary-rollout-in-staging
(make sure folks have the feature flag enabled in staging).

Allison Grant: if you want one-liners for “what’s normal”:
- after weight change, allow ~5–10 mins for metrics to reflect steady state.
- if stickiness on + low QPS, distribution will look lumpy.
- token cost deltas can fluctuate with output length; watch p50/p95 not just mean.

Nadia Rahman: also: “why did guardrail trip unexpectedly” => remind them guardrails evaluate on a rolling window. if they did a big traffic step (10% -> 50% instantly) they can trip due to transient warmup/caching effects.
recommend stepping gradually or enabling timed progression.

Rafael Mendes: (reaction: :thumbsup: x4)

Dev Patel: perfect. i’ll post the draft macro in #support later today for review + we’ll add it to the GA readiness checklist. if anyone has screenshots of the compare view / effective routing preview, drop them here.

Logan Wright: i can grab screenshots from staging dashboards + annotate where variant tags live. will post in a bit.

Sean Gallagher: i’ll send a short “when to page” blurb + what info SRE needs in the escalation (route, rollout id, regions, timestamps).
